newsitem.title: USA: Phillips, Unocal report higher earnings.
newsitem.headline: Phillips, Unocal report higher earnings.

text.p: Two more oil companies reported big increases in third-quarter earnings Wednesday, boosted by surging prices for crude oil and natural gas.
Phillips Petroleum Co., the nation's eighth-largest oil company, said profits rose 38 percent in the quarter and Unocal Corp., the 12th largest, said its profits nearly tripled.
Phillips and Unocal are the latest producers to report higher earnings fuelled by a jump in oil prices that more than offset rising refining costs.

On Monday, Texaco Inc. said earnings jumped 50 percent in the quarter, Chevron Corp. posted a 29 percent gain excluding special items and Exxon Corp., the nation's largest oil company, said profits rose 4 percent.

Crude oil prices have been rising since July on strong demand, especially in the United States, and delays in new world supplies, including postponement of a U.N. plan for Iraq to export oil to buy food and medicine.

Bartlesville, Okla.-based Phillips said net income rose to $187 million, or 71 cents a share, in the quarter, from $136 million, or 52 cents a share, for the same period last year. Sales rose 14 percent to $3.85 billion from $3.37 billion.
"These results continue a trend of strong quarterly earnings in 1996, setting the stage for an outstanding year," Chairman Wayne Allen said in a statement.

Operating earnings in exploration and production nearly doubled as Phillips' average oil price rose $4.90 to $20.54 a barrel and natural gas prices jumped 49 percent. Natural gas production rose 4 percent while crude oil production was flat worldwide.
Refining and marketing earnings fell slightly, as the costs of crude oil feedstock were higher.
Chemical profits fell significantly from last year's strong results, primarily due to lower margins for ethylene, a gas derived from natural gas, and other products.

Unocal, based in El Segundo, Calif., said net income jumped to $171 million, or 69 cents a share, from $59 million, or 20 cents a share, in the year-ago period. Sales grew to $2.61 billion from $2 billion.
Excluding special items from both periods, earnings rose to $153 million, or 61 cents a share, from $50 million, or 17 cents a share.
Unocal cited higher production and energy prices, and said that its West Coast refinery operated more profitably in the quarter.
Phillips stock fell 25 cents to $42.125 and Unocal added 25 cents to $36.625 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
